page: Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 vCPUs across a single physical core with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Cache allocation comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 54 GB of bundled local SSD storage. No hardware graphics accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded compute metrics balanced by low total throughput typical of low-core count systems. The single-core stress-ng benchmark scores in the top 25 percent at 2697.89, while single-core Geekbench performance registers in the middle tier at 1522.0. In contrast, multi-core processing scores—including a Geekbench multi-core result of 1952.0 and PassMark CPU score of 3126.68—rank in the lower tiers due to the hardware constraint of having only two logical execution threads. Large-block uncached memory throughput reaches 34.61 GB/sec for read and 24.14 GB/sec for write operations.

Regarding qualitative cost efficiency, the D2a_v4 presents an entry-level tier configuration that provides direct access to modern AMD architecture for workloads that do not necessitate wide parallel execution. The local 54 GB SSD supplies high-speed ephemeral scratch space, though persistent storage relies on managed block storage volumes. The profile is well suited for small-scale web serving, light background processing, microservices, and development testing environments, whereas high-volume database engines and intensive parallel build systems will be limited by memory bandwidth and core density.
description: The Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading, 8.0 GB of system memory, and 54 GB of bundled local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. The server demonstrates solid single-core execution speed, evidenced by strong stress-ng single-core figures and standard single-threaded compression throughput. However, its multi-core output, memory bandwidth, and raw database operation scores remain restricted by its modest two-thread capacity. Providing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for small-scale applications that do not demand extensive multithreaded scalability. The D2a_v4 is appropriate for lightweight web applications, microservices, non-critical background jobs, and small staging environments.
